title: Kernel oddities and hypotheses - Jasleen
content:
Quick brain dump after the late shift: observed a few small-but-weird kernel-level behaviours that don't match current hypotheses. Put here so I don't lose thread and to leave a clear handoff for morning triage.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Intermittent 20-40ms p99 spikes on short sequences (<=64) on rtx-pool instances around 03:00-04:30 UTC on 2025-11-03.
- Spikes correlate with CPU syscall bursts (see sample trace below) and a small KV-cache eviction wave. Not typical batch/queue backlog.
- Hypotheses: (A) kernel scheduler preemption with high-frequency epoll wake patterns, (B) small-path memcpy/locking contention in the runtime's cache eviction path, (C) hardware thermal throttling coincidentally triggering context switch churn.

Observed evidence:
- p99 timeline (local tracing): 02:58:42 - baseline, 03:07:11 p99 jump to +32ms, 03:09:07 back to baseline, 03:25:03 repeat.
- dmesg snippets: "audit: type=1400 audit(169xxx:xxx): avc:  denied  { getattr } for  pid=..." (no obvious SELinux blocking, just noise).
- perf top during a spike (attached as quick snapshot in run): high on 'do_syscall_64', 'schedule', and small hits on 'memcpy_avx_*'.
- runtime logs: burst of KV-cache eviction logs at the same timestamps (evict_count ~ 318 over 30s).

Quick repro attempt steps I ran (notes):
1) Synthetic replay using small token sequences and interleaved empty requests to emulate tail: ran ./tools/replay --seq-len 32 --qps 120 --concurrency 40 for 15m.
2) Induced cache churn by toggling cache-size from 1GB->600MB in config mid-run (via hot-reload). Saw minor latency shadows but not full spike.
3) Captured perf+ftrace during a reproducer; trace shows many epoll_wait -> do_syscall transitions; syscalls spend microseconds but many in quick succession.

Hypotheses (detailed):
- Hyp A (scheduler preemption + wake storms): If many threads wake (epoll) at near-simultaneous times, scheduler may increase context switches and preemptively push threads off CPU, adding 10-30ms sporadically. Would appear as schedule/do_sched_* in perf.
  - Quick test: pin runtime worker threads to cores (taskset) and re-run replay. If p99 drops -> supports scheduler interaction.
- Hyp B (memcpy/lock hot path during eviction): Eviction path uses a coarse lock and occasionally copies small state chunks; if that hits hot path during many concurrent evicts, tiny serializations add up. Would show content on memcpy symbols and runtime lock contention metrics.
  - Quick test: instrument eviction to use fine-grained locking or bump a counter metric; run with synthetic churn and see lock hold times.
- Hyp C (hardware thermal and frequency scaling): frequency governor sometimes oscillates under bursty CPU use; context switch penalties increase. Check /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/ stats and iostat.
  - Quick test: set governor=performance temporarily and watch p99 over the same reproducer.

Immediate TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] Morning: run pinned-core reproducer (Ishaan can help with taskset flags) and capture perf+ftrace. Expected time: 30-45m. (owner: Ishaan)
- [ ] Add ephemeral metric: eviction_lock_hold_ms with histogram to runtime (small PR). Quick attempt: wrap eviction critical section with timing (owner: me)
- [ ] Temp mitigation: lower eviction aggressiveness threshold by 20% on the affected pool for 24h and monitor p99 (owner: SRE oncall)
- [ ] Try governor=performance on a staging node to rule out freq scaling (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Correlate with infra autoscaler noise: check cluster-level cron jobs (backups, CRON snapshots) at ~03:00 UTC. (owner: me)

Notes-to-self about instrumentation:
- Add fstack-probe in nightly docker image so we can get user+kernel stacks quickly.
- Key perf events: cycles, context-switches, cpu-migrations, syscalls. Save with timestamps aligned to our tracing (trace id).

Open questions:
- Why eviction wave happens in narrow time windows? Is there a global timer or a synchronized TTL expiration across hosts? Follow-up: check codepath that batches TTL sweeps.
- Could a latent bug in prefix cache compaction trigger sudden multi-key eviction (we usually evict per shard but compaction may trigger cross-shard flush)?
- Is there any SLO-based rate limiter kicking in (e.g., to throttle slow clients) that would spike syscalls as we log errors?

Hand-off checklist for morning triage:
- Start with pinned core reproducer -> collect perf/ftrace -> attach symbolized perf report in JIRA INF-3274.
- If pinned test reduces p99 by >15ms -> escalate scheduler hypothesis and open follow-up task to review thread scheduling and affinity.
- If eviction lock shows >2ms hold times during evict wave -> prioritize lock refactor or logging to surface hot-shards.
- If governor toggling helps -> schedule infra change and test wider.

Small notes and shortcuts I left in shell history: (paste these when reproducing)
- ./tools/replay --seq-len 32 --qps 120 --concurrency 40 --duration 900 --tag reproduce-11-03
- perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 120; perf script > /tmp/perf-11-03.out
- sudo trace-cmd record -e sched_switch -e sys_enter -e sys_exit -o /tmp/trace-11-03.dat -- sleep 120

Quick log snippets (copied raw):
- [2025-11-03T03:07:11Z] evict_shard=17 evict_count=318 shard_len_before=412 shard_len_after=94
- [2025-11-03T03:07:11Z] request_id=abcd node=rtx-12 latency_ms=44 seq_len=12
- [2025-11-03T03:07:12Z] perf sample: top symbols: schedule, do_syscall_64, memcpy_avx_256

Final: keep it simple in triage. Don't over-optimize. First figure out if problem is CPU scheduling or application-level lock. If both small wins stack: bump eviction metric, reduce aggressiveness, pin cores temporarily.

If anyone reads this in the morning and wants to pick up: start with pinned-core reproducer, attach perf, paste outputs into INF-3274 and tag me (@jasleen). I'll be online for the 09:30 sync.

Random idea (throwaway): try switching runtime worker threading model from N threads to N/2 with wider batching to see if fewer context switches reduces tail. Can be quick A/B on canary.

-- Jasleen
